protocol_rpc.WARNING: These are SYMBOLIC KEY NAMES of the private config map protocol.rpc. Their values (Google batchexecute rpc ids) are NOT in the extension and NOT recovered here. Do not substitute any guess.
protocol_rpc.type_required: string (typeof === 'string'); only the 7 health keys are type-checked at health time

protocol_other.value_status: must equal 1 to be usable by client 1.3.138

schema_wire.note: ToolFlow reads ONLY these two keys of schema.wire. Any other wire fields (prompt position, ratio enums, model keys, etc.) exist only inside the opaque schema object passed to Bridge and are NOT consumable from client code.

aspect_ratios.type: object keyed by ratio string (hasOwnProperty); value opaque (video edit path uses truthiness)

fields.rule: key = model value; or entry whose ui_values[] contains the canonical/UI value (case-insensitive trim)
shallow-merged over model entry for video
_capabilityModel resolves to a model key string (opaque, passed to Bridge only via models)

state_mapping.opaque: Everything else in state_mapping is passed to Bridge untouched (stateMapping param) and into the config fingerprint. State names ToolFlow understands in Bridge OUTPUT: see poll outputs[].state. Bridge attaches rawState/unknownState itself.

fields.consumer: V2 slot / ref validation concurrency / gateway api concurrency min(4,x)

fields.constraint: integer 3000..60000 else Bridge reconnect timeout falls back to 10000

runtime.note: video_timeout_ms <= 7200000 is asserted in doc 05 but not located in this pass (UNVERIFIED here).

error_mapping.match: case-insensitive startsWith over candidates [providerErrorCodes..., error.code, grpcReason]; longest key wins; value is passed to FlowApiAdapter.classifyError('', value); result 'unknown' is ignored

gate_order.check: BridgeClient.ping installed; all required capabilities present (re-ping once with force)

client_side.command_id: commandId (v2-client-...) is the idempotency/receipt key; Google has no idempotency key in this contract

upscale_receipt.note: No receipt-recovery for flow_v2_upscale_*; ambiguous stays ambiguous

batchexecute_transport.meaning: URL PATH(S) the MAIN-world observer hooks (XHR+fetch). Path regex /^\/(?:[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\/)*[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$/, <=8 paths, <=256 chars, no 'u/<n>' segment. Path only: host is the flow page origin (flow.google.com / labs.google page context) - the config carries no host, so full URL host is NOT asserted.
batchexecute_transport.request_body_parse: f.req (FormData | URLSearchParams | bytes | string) = JSON; envelope[0] = array of rows; row[0]=rpcId string, row[1]=payload (JSON string, parsed). This is classic Google batchexecute: rpcIds in requests are the REAL ids but are NOT present in any config we hold.
batchexecute_transport.response_frame_parse: frames where frame[0]=='wrb.fr', frame[1]=rpcId string (/^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}$/), frame[2]=JSON string payload; node[5] also read as payload for error matching.
batchexecute_transport.delivery_to_observer: FlowObserverConfigRelay.publish reads tool_provider_api_configs.flow_v2_observer_transport & native_project_media_identity and dispatches CustomEvents TOOL_FLOW_OBSERVER_TRANSPORT / TOOL_FLOW_NATIVE_MEDIA_SCHEMA
batchexecute_transport.relation_to_bridge: INFERENCE only: Bridge path/rpc used by flow_v2_* is not shown; the observer path is what the page's own traffic uses. protocol.rpc.* ids remain unknown.

media_identity.how_applied: For every wrb.fr frame: body=JSON.parse(frame[2]); rows=body at collection_path. Row accepted iff uuid=row@uuid_path is UUID, row@project_path (lowercased) == project id from the page URL, row@generation_path is UUID, row@details_path is an array, and uuid evidence exists. Then media_types[].rules decide image vs video; asb_url_paths locate AB-… (ASB) URL strings which map ASB alias <-> UUID.
media_identity.video_rules: (row[7][1][0] and row[7][1][1] positive integers) OR (row[5][6][1][0][0] string AND row[5][8][0] integer)
media_identity.validation: validateMediaSchema: exactly keys version,enabled,collection_path,uuid_path,project_path,generation_path,details_path,media_types; paths length 1..8 ints 0..128; media_types exactly {image,video}; rules<=8; kinds string|integer|positive_integer|positive_integer_pair
media_identity.limits: This is the shape of NATIVE page responses the observer reads. It does not describe flow_v2_* Bridge outputs, which return UUID operationId/mediaId.

media_url_route.note: tRPC redirect used to serve media by UUID name (public config + FlowApiAdapter anchor); different from batchexecute
